_comment: Tier-2 fixture: SolverCG fails on an INDEFINITE matrix. This is the canonical Stokes / Helmholtz pitfall: 'System is INDEFINITE — cannot use SolverCG, use SolverGMRES / SolverMinRes / a direct solver. Signal: SolverCG reports breakdown on iteration 2-3 with a negative inner product, before the iterative residual has dropped at all.' We build a tiny 2x2 indefinite SparseMatrix in deal.II and ask SolverCG to solve it.MUTATION CONTROL (2026-08-07): MUTATION APPLIED AND IT DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE. The T2_MUTATE=1 hook is left in source.cpp so the negative result stays re-runnable, but NO _mutation recipe is declared: a declared recipe that survives reads as a defect rather than as the finding it is (same treatment as dune/point_indicator_selects_no_facet and febio/static_activation_ramp_shape_does_not_matter). Re-run by hand from the fixture directory after any harness run has built it: `T2_MUTATE=1 ./_build/prog`. The hook sets the second diagonal entry to +1, making the matrix diag(1, 1), which is SPD — the indefiniteness the fixture is named for is gone. Measured 2026-08-07: CG converges and the program prints "SolverCG converged on indefinite matrix in 1 iterations — pitfall claim does not hold for this build" and exits 2, and the fixture STILL PASSES, because its single expectation is "SolverCG" and that sentence contains it. The expectation is therefore satisfied by output whose own words say the pitfall was NOT reproduced. On the exception path the same string is supplied twice over, by the fixture's own "SolverCG raised: " prefix and by deal.II's exception text, so it can never go missing. The fix would be an expectation naming the measured value; it is deliberately NOT made here, because tuning a fixture until its mutation goes red is how a mutation control stops being evidence.
